description: Ground truth for the PolkaVM / pallet-revive PoC fixtures. Every vulnerable contract COMPILES with resolc (verified in F0) and triggers one PolkaVM 'difference-with-EVM' check (class B: silent runtime difference). The class-A file documents resolc's compile-time rejection and is NOT placed on the scan path.

expected.rationale: PolkaVM does not apply the 63/64 gas rule; forwarding all gas to an untrusted callee is a DoS vector.
Fixed 128kb memory buffer; a caller-controlled unbounded allocation can trap at runtime (OutOfBound).
new Child{salt:...}() is a CREATE2 deployment; on PolkaVM the derived address differs from the EVM derivation.
type(T).creationCode returns a keccak256 hash on PolkaVM, so EVM CREATE2 precomputation is wrong.
block.prevrandao translates to a constant (2500000000000000) on PolkaVM; randomness derived from it is predictable.
With via-ir (how resolc compiles), base constructors run before derived state-var initializers; init-order-dependent logic changes value vs EVM.

selfdestruct compiles under resolc (verified); flagged because its runtime behaviour on pallet-revive may differ from the EVM (runtime semantics not independently confirmed); portability/semantic risk.

error_cases.resolc_error: LLVM IR generator: The `EXTCODECOPY` instruction is not supported
error_cases.note: Difference class (A): resolc rejects it at compile time. This is the compiler's job, not a MIESC finding; the file must NOT be placed on the normal scan path.
